# Comwit Template — agent guide

`create-comwit` scaffolds a Next.js 16 project whose structure is the documentation:
services sliced by domain, four layers that depend one way, an `.ai.md` rulebook beside
every layer, Storybook for page-level review, and skills for the one-time setups. Two
positions: AI-native (the rules an agent needs ship with the project) and Next.js as the
full stack (the api layer is the backend). All Comwit guides: https://library.comwit.io/llms.txt

## Create a project

```bash
npm create comwit@latest my-app     # or: npx create-comwit@latest my-app
cd my-app && pnpm run dev
```

Flags: `--opennext` (Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext: wrangler.jsonc, open-next.config.ts, `preview`/`deploy` scripts) ·
`--name <pkg>` · `--pm pnpm|npm|yarn|bun` · `--no-install` · `--no-git` · `--dry`.

Already have a Next.js project? See "Migrate an existing project" below.

## Inside a generated project

Read these before writing code, in this order:

1. `AGENTS.md` — the rules file (CLAUDE.md imports it): flow, stack, tree, env, database/storage/deploy.
2. `src/services/.ai.md` — import rules and layer dependencies.
3. The `.ai.md` of the layer you are about to touch: `src/services/api.ai.md`,
   `src/services/state.ai.md`, `src/services/page.ai.md`, `src/server/repository/.ai.md`,
   `src/app/.ai.md`, `src/services/admin/.ai.md`.
4. `src/services/design.md` before any visual decision, then `.storybook/stories/.ai.md`
   before any screen work.

Dependency flow `page → state → api → repository`; write order is the reverse. All data
goes through `src/server/repository/` (in-memory rows in `_data/` until a database is
connected; connecting one changes only repository bodies). The api layer's `'use server'`
functions are wrapped in `createAction` and exported through `resolveActions`; the build
turns them into the kit's own transport (one POST route handler, parallel calls, only
`ActionError` messages reach the browser), not native Server Actions — keep the source
convention and call the api only through a domain's `index.ts`. Server settings are
getters on `src/server/config.ts` that read the environment on access.

Storybook (`pnpm storybook`, http://localhost:6006) runs the real pages inside their
service layouts with the real state and actions; only the api layer's public objects are
replaced by the mocks in `.storybook/mocks/api/{service}-{domain}.ts`. Stories are
page-level, one file per page under `.storybook/stories/{service}/`, states as named
exports, sidebar order design system → user type → page. A missing mock or a server
import fails the Storybook build, never the app: `pnpm validate:storybook` and
`pnpm build-storybook` stay separate from `pnpm run validate`.

Skills in `.agents/skills/`: `app-setup` (tabs, detail screens, PWA — before the first app
screen), `auth-setup` (Better Auth per service — after a database), `seo-optimize`.
`pnpm run validate` after every change; the Oxlint rules in `eslint-rules/` enforce every
boundary above.

## Migrate an existing project

Use this when a Next.js App Router project already exists and should end up like a
generated one: the same layers, rule files, lint rules, shared code, comwit-ui
components, design system and Storybook. The goal is the template's structure, not a
thin layer over the old code. Work through every step; be as thorough as each step says.
A Pages Router project moves to the App Router first; that migration is not covered here.

### 1. Scaffold the reference into a temporary folder, outside the project

```bash
REF="$(mktemp -d)/comwit-ref"
npx create-comwit@latest "$REF" --no-install --no-git   # add --opennext when the project deploys to Cloudflare Workers
```

Never scaffold into the project (the CLI refuses a non-empty directory). Treat `$REF`
as read-only reference material, keep it until the last step, then delete it.
`npx create-comwit@latest x --dry` lists every file it would write.

### 2. Inventory the project before changing anything

Write down, in a scratch note: package manager; Next.js version; `src/` or not; import
alias; tsconfig (decorators?); lint tool and config; test runner; CI commands; ORM and
database; auth; object storage; hosting; env/config module; UI library, Tailwind version,
tokens, fonts; locale and timezone; how data is fetched and cached today (SWR, React
Query, Redux, fetch in effects, Server Actions); existing agent files (AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions); and every route with the
components and utils it uses. The route list drives steps 6–8.

### 3. Rule files: copy them, then rewrite every line that is not true here

From `$REF`: `AGENTS.md` (merge into the existing rules file, do not overwrite; keep
one canonical file and make `CLAUDE.md` import it with `@AGENTS.md`),
`.agents/rules/project-instructions.md` (Antigravity only), `src/services/.ai.md`,
`src/services/api.ai.md`, `src/services/state.ai.md`, `src/services/page.ai.md`,
`src/services/design.md`, `src/services/admin/.ai.md` (only with an operator service),
`src/app/.ai.md`, `src/server/repository/.ai.md`, `.storybook/stories/.ai.md`, and the
comments of `.env.example` (never `.env`). Each `.ai.md` sits beside the folder it
governs.

Adapt: the package manager and every command; folder names and the alias; the tech
stack table (database, auth, storage, deploy, lint runner); the locale (Korean UI copy
and the KST time helpers become the project's); `design.md`'s project concept, filled
with the real brand (voice, mood, tokens, fonts); and remove the sections for things the
project will not adopt, writing the decision into `AGENTS.md`. When you are done, every
path named in a copied file exists in the project.

### 4. Lint rules: copy `eslint-rules/`, `.oxlintrc.json` and `scripts/lint.mjs`

- The rules use the ESLint rule API. Run them with Oxlint through the copied
  `.oxlintrc.json` (recommended), or register `eslint-rules/index.cjs` as a local plugin
  in an ESLint flat config and copy the `custom/*` entries into its rules. Keep the
  project's existing rules.
- The rules assume `src/app`, `src/services/{service}/{api,state,page}/{domain}`,
  `src/server/repository`, the `@/` alias and `@/lib/components/ui`. Move the code to
  that layout rather than editing path constants; if a constant must change, change the
  rule, its message and the matching `.ai.md` together.
- Classify every rule as adopted, adapted or dropped, with the reason in `AGENTS.md`.
  Infra-tied rules: `drizzle-node-config` (Drizzle only); `better-auth-required-options`
  and `auth-hydration-boundary` (the Better Auth `getMe()` boundary); `no-db-in-api` and
  `server-only-import` (keep; point the database import pattern at the project's ORM);
  `api-structure`, `api-create-action`, `api-action-error`, `api-only-server-action` and
  `server-actions` (need the transport from step 5); `server-config-getters` (needs
  `src/server/config.ts`); `no-native-interactive` (needs the comwit-ui components);
  `no-next-image` and `no-anchor-tag` (template opinions: keep or drop deliberately).
- Run lint over the whole project once. A rule with existing violations starts as
  `warn` and becomes `error` when its layer is migrated. Add a `validate` script
  (typecheck + lint), keep the project's scripts, and put `validate` in CI.
- Prove that every adopted custom rule fires: write a deliberate violation in a scratch
  file, see the error, delete the file.

### 5. Shared code: bring `src/lib` and `src/server` scaffolding, replace the equivalents

Copy from `$REF` and wire. Where the project has its own version of the same thing,
replace it with the template's and delete the old one; never keep two.

- `src/lib/utils/` (`cn`, `createAction`, `resolveActions`, `ActionError`, the http
  client), `src/lib/popup.tsx`, `src/lib/interaction.ts`, `src/lib/overlay-motion.tsx`,
  `src/lib/ui-text.ts`, `src/lib/kst.ts` (or a locale-correct equivalent),
  `src/lib/admin-routes.ts` (with an admin service).
- The api transport: `src/lib/server-action/`, `next.config.ts` exported through
  `withServerFn(...)`, the `imports["#comwit-server-fn-runtime"]` map in `package.json`,
  `src/app/api/internal/server-fn/[...slug]/route.ts` and the `ssr-bridge` import in the
  root layout. Adopt it whole or do not adopt the api rules; not half.
- State wiring: `@comwit/state` installed, `experimentalDecorators` and
  `emitDecoratorMetadata` in tsconfig, `src/lib/state/` (StateProvider) and
  `src/lib/layout/` (StateProvider, OverlayProvider, Toaster) mounted once in the root
  layout, with a `<Suspense fallback={null}>` around the routed content.
- `src/server/config.ts` as getters, `src/server/repository/{types.ts,id.ts,schema.dbml}`
  and `_data/`; the repository rules rewritten around the project's ORM.
- Service worker, offline page, version guard and `scripts/*.mjs`: only when the product
  wants PWA behaviour.
- Versions: keep the project's Next.js (never downgrade it); install the kit packages at
  the pins in `$REF/package.json`; copy `pnpm-workspace.yaml` if pnpm's minimum release
  age blocks them.

### 6. UI: install comwit-ui and replace the project's components with it

- `npx comwit-ui@latest init` (`--locale ko` only for Korean UI) with aliases that match
  the project; it writes `comwit.json`, `comwit-tokens.css` and the base dependencies.
  Set `--font-pretendard` on `<html>` or the project's font.
- For every component in the inventory with a comwit-ui equivalent (button, input,
  text-field, select, dialog, sheet, bottom-sheet, form, data-table, toast, popup, tabs,
  dropdown-menu, …): `npx comwit-ui@latest add <name>`, port every call site, delete the
  old component. Keep a project-specific component only when nothing in the kit covers
  it, and then rebuild it from kit parts and tokens inside `src/lib/components/`.
- Libraries the kit wraps (sonner, overlay-kit, react-hook-form, TanStack Table, tiptap,
  react-day-picker, SSGOI) are used through the kit's files, never imported directly.
- Move the brand into token overrides in `globals.css`, then delete the old theme and
  global styles. Guide: https://library.comwit.io/ui/llms.txt

### 7. Design system: apply `design.md` to everything you touch

- Before any screen: fill the project concept in `design.md` (voice, mood) from the
  existing brand, and map every visual decision to a token (`--brand`, `--radius-scale`,
  `--display-font`, …) set in `globals.css`. Components are edited last.
- Every migrated screen is restyled to `design.md`, not reproduced in new components:
  tokens instead of hardcoded colours and sizes, `px-gutter` for page margins, one message
  per section, no eyebrows or helper captions, no muted body text, no card stacking, UI
  copy in `ui-text.ts`. Behaviour (gestures, scroll, focus, IME) stays in the kit.

### 8. Screens and data: move to services and domains, one domain at a time

- Order inside a domain: `repository → api → state → page`, as `src/services/.ai.md`
  says. Start with the domain behind the first route in the inventory; finish it (lint
  clean, story written, old files deleted) before the next.
- repository: every data access becomes `src/server/repository/{entity}.ts` on the
  project's real database (`server-only`, soft delete, uuid v7 ids). The api never
  touches the database.
- api: one domain per screen, `createAction` + `resolveActions`, `ActionError`,
  screen-shaped responses with display labels; route handlers and client `fetch` calls
  are replaced by api calls through state.
- state: SWR, React Query, Redux and effect-based fetching are replaced by `@comwit/state`
  domain hooks (`types.ts → model.ts → actions/*.ts → index.ts`); side effects (toast,
  popup, navigation) move into actions. Guide: https://library.comwit.io/state/llms.txt
- page: `src/services/{service}/page/{route}/` split into sections, `'use client'`,
  `<Link>` for internal links, `<img>` instead of `next/image`; `src/app` routes only
  import pages.
- Existing auth: keep it, and implement the `getMe()` + hydration adapter boundary from
  `page.ai.md` on top of it; run `auth-setup` only when adopting Better Auth on Drizzle.
- Delete the old folder as each domain lands; the same screen never lives in two places.

### 9. Storybook: set it up from `$REF`, write a story per migrated page

- Copy `.storybook/` (main.ts, preview.tsx, preview.css, next.config.ts, tsconfig.json,
  api-mocks.mjs, mocks/, stories/shell.tsx, stories/.ai.md, the design-system story),
  `.agents/tests/storybook-api-mocks.test.mjs`, the `storybook`, `validate:storybook` and
  `build-storybook` scripts and the `storybook`, `@storybook/nextjs-vite` and `vite`
  devDependencies. Exclude `.storybook` and `storybook-static` from the app tsconfig,
  add the `.storybook/**` override to `.oxlintrc.json`, gitignore `storybook-static/`.
- Adapt `stories/shell.tsx` to the project's real service layouts and `mocks/session.ts`
  to its user type.
- For every migrated page: one story file under `stories/{service}/`, real layout,
  states as named exports, the api mocked in `mocks/api/{service}-{domain}.ts`. Extend
  the design-system overview with the project's tokens and controls.
- `pnpm validate:storybook` and `pnpm build-storybook` pass and stay separate from
  `validate`.

### 10. Skills and agent config

Copy only the skills that apply, each with its `.claude/skills/<name>/` stub,
`.agents/scripts/cleanup-skill.mjs`, `.agents/tests/skills.test.mjs` and the
`agents:test` script: `app-setup` for app-like products without a shell yet,
`auth-setup` only when adopting Better Auth on Drizzle, `seo-optimize` in most projects.
Rewrite their text for the project's package manager and paths.

### 11. Finish

- `validate`, `agents:test`, `validate:storybook`, `build-storybook` and the production
  build pass; every adopted lint rule has been proven to fire.
- Grep the copied files for `pnpm`, `Drizzle`, `Better Auth`, `/관리자`, `KST`, `my-app`,
  `src/services`, `comwit-ui` and `.storybook`, and resolve every hit deliberately.
- Delete `$REF`. Record in `AGENTS.md`: the template version and date adopted, what was
  adapted or skipped and why, and the backlog of domains not moved yet.
- Report what was replaced, what was kept and what is left.

Prompt to hand an agent:

```text
Read https://library.comwit.io/template/llms.txt. This is an existing Next.js project.
Follow "Migrate an existing project" as thoroughly as it says: scaffold the template
into a temporary folder outside this repo with create-comwit; bring over the rule files
(AGENTS.md, every .ai.md, design.md, skills), the eslint-rules and lint config, the
shared lib code, the comwit-ui components and the Storybook setup; then refactor this
project to the template's structure, replacing our components and utils with the
template's, applying the design system to every screen you touch and writing stories as
you go. Adapt every copied file to this project's real package manager, folder layout,
database, auth, storage, hosting and locale; leave no template default that is not true
here. Finish with validate, agents:test and build-storybook passing, and report what was
replaced, what was kept and what is left.
```

## Reference

- Why domains, not layers: https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/architecture
- Folder structure and lint rules: https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/structure
- Design decisions (server-function transport, caching, auth boundary): https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/decisions
- The four layers: https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/layers
- Agents, guides, Storybook and skills: https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/agents
- Migration guide for humans: https://library.comwit.io/template/docs/migrate
- State library: https://library.comwit.io/state/llms.txt
- UI library: https://library.comwit.io/ui/llms.txt
- All guides: https://library.comwit.io/llms.txt
